---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: CashBackedBookToMarket
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), NEG(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)))
HYPOTHESIS: Cheapness earns a premium only when reported profits are backed by operating cash; cheap firms whose earnings come from accruals are value traps, so the joint rank of high book-to-market and low total accruals predicts returns better than either leg alone.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Book-to-market captures mispricing of hard assets while total accruals (ib minus oancf, scaled by assets) captures earnings-quality risk that keeps the discount justified. Ranking both channels and summing isolates firms that are simultaneously cheap and cash-backed, which should carry the highest expected return.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: ValueGatedByNegativeAccruals
EXPRESSION: MUL(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), INDICATOR(NEG(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), 0))
HYPOTHESIS: The value premium is concentrated in the subsample where accruals are negative (cash flow exceeds earnings); for accrual-heavy firms cheapness carries no premium, so a hard accounting-quality gate on the value signal should sharpen both the cross-sectional slope and the long-short alpha.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The indicator switches the valuation signal on only for conservatively-reporting firms, effectively setting accrual-inflated cheap stocks to zero exposure rather than shorting them. This conditional structure tests whether the value premium is state-dependent on accounting quality rather than additively adjusted by it.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: AccrualPurgedBookValueYield
EXPRESSION: RATIO(SUB(ceq, TS_SUM(SUB(ib, oancf), 3)), MUL(prcc_f, csho))
HYPOTHESIS: Book equity built up by three years of cumulative accruals is soft capital that will be reversed or written off; removing cumulative accruals from the numerator yields a "cash-verified" book value whose ratio to market price is a cleaner measure of true cheapness.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This restates the valuation ratio itself rather than combining two scores, so accruals enter as a balance-sheet correction to the value anchor. Firms with high purged book-to-market are cheap on assets that have been validated by cash generation, and should outperform nominally cheap firms whose equity is accrual residue.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: CheapWithImprovingAccrualQuality
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), NEG(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Among cheap firms, the direction of accrual quality matters more than its level: a falling accrual ratio signals that earnings are converting into cash and that the market's discount is about to be resolved upward.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: EBITDA-to-price provides a cash-oriented cheapness measure, while the year-over-year decline in accrual intensity captures a transition from aggressive to conservative reporting. The interaction targets cheap firms in the process of accounting repair, a state ignored by static accrual levels.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: ValueTrapAccrualToPrice
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(DELTA(wcap, 1), MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))))
HYPOTHESIS: Working-capital accruals capitalized per dollar of market value are most dangerous exactly where the stock looks cheap: high book-to-market firms funding reported profits with receivable and inventory build-ups are distressed value traps that subsequently underperform.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: Scaling the working-capital accrual by market equity (not assets) makes it a valuation-relative quality measure, and multiplying by the book-to-market rank concentrates the signal in the cheap segment where accrual reversal is least buffered by growth. The product should predict low returns, giving the interaction an explicitly negative sign.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: PersistentCashBackingEarningsYield
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(ib, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), TS_SUM(INDICATOR(SUB(oancf, ib), 0), 5))
HYPOTHESIS: A single year of clean accruals can be noise; a five-year count of years in which operating cash flow exceeded reported income measures durable conservatism, and high earnings yield combined with persistent cash backing identifies genuinely mispriced firms rather than temporarily flattered ones.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The indicator-sum converts accrual quality into a persistence state, filtering out firms whose good accrual year is transitory. Pairing this with earnings-to-price makes the value signal credible only when the earnings stream has repeatedly been validated by cash.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---CRITIQUE CashBackedBookToMarket---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: This is a plain equal-weight rank sum of two of the most heavily published anomalies (book-to-market and Sloan total accruals) with no conditioning or novel construction, so it is a rediscovery of the standard "value plus earnings-quality" composite rather than a genuine cross-theme insight.

---CRITIQUE ValueGatedByNegativeAccruals---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: The hard indicator gate zeroes roughly half the universe, creating a large mass point that will dominate the low-signal buckets and make the short leg an uninterpretable mixture of gated firms, negative-book firms, and genuine growth stocks, so the portfolio test cannot cleanly identify the claimed state dependence.

---CRITIQUE AccrualPurgedBookValueYield---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 4
RATIONALE: Embedding the accrual correction inside the book-value anchor (cash-verified equity over market cap) is a substantively different construction from an ex-post rank blend and has a coherent balance-sheet story, though the reviewer should note it decomposes exactly into B/M minus price-scaled cumulative accruals and so still shares variance with both parent anomalies.

---CRITIQUE CheapWithImprovingAccrualQuality---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The sign of the accrual-change leg is economically ambiguous — a falling (ib − oancf)/at can equally reflect deteriorating income as improving cash conversion — so the hypothesis of "accounting repair" is not what the expression reliably measures, and the wrapper is otherwise the same additive value-plus-accruals rank sum as the first proposal.

---CRITIQUE ValueTrapAccrualToPrice---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: The rank product makes the low-signal (long) leg an incoherent mix of low-accrual value firms and high-accrual growth firms, and the premise contradicts the documented concentration of accrual mispricing in glamour/low-B/M stocks, so the negative expected sign is poorly supported by the expression's actual cross-sectional structure.

---CRITIQUE PersistentCashBackingEarningsYield---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The five-year count of cash-backed earnings years is a genuinely different, noise-robust way to measure durable conservatism (closer in spirit to a persistence state than to a level accrual), but the discrete 0–5 support creates heavy rank ties and the earnings-yield leg plus five-year history requirement will strain coverage, so this is worth testing only if the persistence term is shown to add over the one-year accrual level.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: CashVersusEarningsValueGap
EXPRESSION: SUB(IND_RANK(RATIO(oancf, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_RANK(RATIO(ib, MUL(prcc_f, csho))))
HYPOTHESIS: Investors anchor valuation on reported earnings rather than cash flow, so firms that rank cheap on operating-cash-flow yield but only mediocre on earnings yield are systematically underpriced; the divergence between the two valuation rankings, measured within industry, is the mispricing rather than either level.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
REASONING: Instead of adding a value score to an accrual score, this measures the same firm's position in two competing valuation ladders whose only difference is the accrual component of income, so the signal is zero by construction when earnings are fully cash-backed. Industry ranking removes sector-level differences in normal accrual intensity and in typical multiples, isolating firms whose price reflects accrual-laden earnings instead of the cash they actually generate.

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: AccrualGradedValue
EXPRESSION: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 1), RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at))))
HYPOTHESIS: The value premium scales continuously with accounting conservatism: book-to-market should be discounted in proportion to how accrual-dependent reported income is, so weighting cheapness by the firm's percentile of accrual conservatism produces a monotone "credible value" signal.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: Replacing the hard indicator with a [0,1] cross-sectional percentile removes the mass point at zero, so the low-signal bucket is populated by genuinely expensive or accrual-inflated firms rather than a mixture of gated names. Winsorizing book-to-market keeps distressed and near-zero-price observations from dominating the product while preserving full coverage of the value dimension.

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: CheapAtCashConversionPeak
EXPRESSION: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 1), TS_RANK(RATIO(oancf, ebitda), 5))
HYPOTHESIS: Cash conversion of pre-accrual profitability (oancf divided by ebitda) is an unambiguous accrual-quality state: when a cheap firm sits near the top of its own five-year cash-conversion history, its depressed multiple reflects stale accrual skepticism that is being resolved by realized cash.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: Using ebitda as the denominator fixes the sign ambiguity the critic raised, since a rising ratio cannot be produced by falling income the way a falling (ib − oancf)/at can. The self-referenced TS_RANK converts accrual quality into a firm-specific state variable and gates the EBITDA-to-price cheapness signal, so the interaction is dynamic and conditional rather than an additive rank sum.

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: GlamourAccrualOverstatement
EXPRESSION: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1), IND_RANK(RATIO(MUL(prcc_f, csho), ceq)))
HYPOTHESIS: Accrual mispricing is concentrated where expectations are extrapolated: highly valued (low book-to-market) firms that report income unsupported by operating cash flow face the largest subsequent earnings disappointment and negative returns, while the same accruals in cheap firms are already priced.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: This reverses the earlier premise to match the documented concentration of the accrual anomaly in glamour stocks, using an industry-ranked price-to-book gate in [0,1] that amplifies accruals for expensive firms and shrinks them toward zero for value firms. The high-signal (short) leg is therefore unambiguously accrual-heavy glamour, and the low-signal (long) leg is cash-generating glamour plus neutral value names, giving an interpretable spread with a clean negative expected sign.
